title: Enforce the order lifecycle as a state machine
prompt:
Order in shop/orders.py lets any lifecycle method run from any status, so we have refunded orders that were never paid. Please turn it into a proper state machine following docs/ORDER_LIFECYCLE.md (transition table, terminal states, the 30-day refund window, and the tracking-number and reason rules).

API changes in shop/orders.py:

- Order(order_id, items, clock=None). clock is a zero-argument callable returning the current datetime; the default returns the current time as a timezone-aware UTC datetime. Every timestamp (history entries, delivered_at, the refund-window check) comes from clock().
- A new exception InvalidTransition(Exception) with attributes .state (the order's status when the call was made) and .event (the event name, e.g. "ship"). It is raised when an event is not allowed from the current status, including any event from a terminal status and a refund after the 30-day window.
- ship() and cancel() raise ValueError for a missing tracking number or reason, but the status check comes first: an event that is not allowed raises InvalidTransition whatever its argument.
- A call that raises changes nothing: status, history, tracking_number and cancel_reason stay as they were.
- order.history: a list, empty for a new order, with one entry appended per successful transition. Each entry is a Transition, a typing.NamedTuple defined in shop/orders.py with fields (event, from_state, to_state, at), where at is clock() at the time of the transition.
- order.delivered_at: None until deliver() succeeds, then the clock time of delivery.
- order.is_terminal: a property, True in cancelled and refunded.
- order.can(event): whether that event name would be allowed right now (ignoring ship/cancel arguments, but including the refund window). Unknown event names give False.
- order.allowed_events(): the allowed event names, sorted alphabetically.

order.status keeps its current string values, and shop/reports.py and the tests in tests/ should keep working.
acceptance: Allowed and rejected transitions per the table with InvalidTransition.state/.event; shipped orders cannot be cancelled or refunded; terminal states; ValueError for missing tracking number or reason after the status check; stripping; refund window inclusive at 30 days via injected clock; history Transition entries with clock times and nothing recorded on failure; delivered_at; default clock UTC-aware; can() and allowed_events().
difficulty_rationale: A transition table plus guards, history and an injected clock, with several edge cases around ordering of checks and failed calls.
